lots.what_it_is: Framed colour print after Salvador Dali, 'The Discovery of America by Christopher Columbus', numbered XVI/CCC, with 'Diego Colon, Marques de Aguilafuente' stamp and 'Colon' signature, a pencil Dali-style signature, and two inset 1893 Columbian Exposition half dollars

lots.dropped_entries: None to drop; researcher supplied no entries.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3: pencil 'XVI/CCC' lower left; circular ink stamp 'DIEGO COLON / MARQUES DE AGUILAFUENTE' with a coat of arms and an ink 'Colon' signature crossing it. Photo 4: pencil Dali-style signature lower right. Photo 5: two 1893 Columbian Exposition half dollars, one obverse (Columbus head, heavily toned), one reverse (Santa Maria, '1893'), both circulated. Stamp by a Columbus descendant suggests a Columbus quincentenary (c.1992) commemorative edition; Dali died in January 1989, so a hand signature on a sheet printed after then cannot be his. Whether this sheet predates his death is unknown.
lots.condition: Sheet looks clean and flat in the photos, fresh white mount, brushed silver frame. Coins circulated with toning.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there a certificate, publisher's blind stamp or documentation giving the publisher and year of printing? Is the lower right signature in pencil or printed? Are the coins genuine silver 1893 half dollars and are they removable?
